findings.title: `cf config unset --project` cannot remove a personal key from the shared file; the collision fix and walkthrough step 9 fail as written
`migrate-personal` and the checker rule need direct file access that the "no API change" contract doesn't provide
findings.description:
Lines 49 and 181 say the `ConfigManager` public API is unchanged, and line 61 says the only new export is the path helper. But both new features need things the public API can't give them:
- `migrate-personal` (line 144) must read the raw shared file, write the personal file, and delete from the **shared** file. `get` returns only the merged value, and `delete(key,'project')` routes to the personal file.
- The `ConsistencyChecker` rule (line 142) must read the raw shared file.

`readToml`/`resolveKey`/`deleteKey` are private to the module (`ConfigManager.ts:21-89`). `ConfigManager.projectPath` is `private` (`ConfigManager.ts:115`). So the CLI command and the checker can't do this without a new method or newly exported helpers, such as `ConfigManager.migratePersonalKeys()` returning a per-key result, or `listMisplacedPersonalKeys()`. The design should name that method, its return shape (moved / skipped / failed per key), and where the per-key logic lives (core vs CLI).

findings.title: The checker rule's placement and scan path are unspecified; the "exactly one warning" criterion fails for projects with worktrees
findings.description:
`ConsistencyChecker` has two entry points: `check()`, which runs per-slice rules only (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:53-73`), and `checkAll()`. The design doesn't say which one runs the rule. `cf check --slice` and `workflow_check` with `sliceIndex` call `check()` (`check.ts:220`, `workflowTools.ts:288`), so the rule's visibility depends on that choice.

The design also doesn't say which `projectPath` gets scanned. Both `cf check` and `workflow_check` build one view per worktree, and when worktrees exist they **exclude the main checkout** (`check.ts:210-213`, `workflowTools.ts:278-281`):
- If the rule scans `view.projectPath`, a committed shared file present in N worktrees produces N findings. Each has a different `location`, so the rule+location+description dedup doesn't collapse them, which contradicts line 217 ("exactly one"). The main checkout is never scanned at all.
- If the rule uses the injected `ConfigManager`'s path (main checkout), it needs an accessor that doesn't exist. `config` is also optional (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:47`).

Separately, line 142 says the rule is added "alongside the existing config-hygiene-style checks". No such checks exist. Every current rule is about documents or worktrees.

findings.title: Worktrees: the personal file is per-checkout, but readers use the main checkout's path
findings.description:
Line 111 justifies `personal` with "per-developer/per-worktree git topology". The paths don't line up:
- `cf config set ... --project` run from a worktree resolves the project through `resolveProject(..., worktreeId)`, which overlays `projectPath = worktreePath` (`config.ts:23-25`, `worktree-overlay.ts:9`). The write therefore goes to `<worktree>/.context-forge.local.toml`.
- The guide branch guard (`guides.ts:171`, `ctx.projectPath` is the main project path per `guides.ts:46`), `cf check`, `cf next`, `cf status` and `workflow_*` all build `ConfigManager` with the **main** `project.projectPath`.

Before this slice, a committed shared value showed up in every worktree through git. After migration, the gitignored local file exists only in the checkout where it was written. Two things follow:
- A value set from a worktree is never seen by the branch guard (`branchGuard.ts:83-85`).
- A value set in the main checkout isn't present in the worktree's own files.

This silently weakens the 916 guardrail. The design needs to say which checkout's local file is authoritative, and whether the CLI should resolve config through the main project path.

findings.title: Existing installations never get the `.gitignore` line, so the slice's core goal isn't met for them
findings.description:
The gitignore line is only written by `cf init` (lines 32 and 159). Existing projects were already initialised and have no reason to re-run it. Projects created through `cf worktree init` never run it either (`init.ts:71-74` returns early). In those projects, `cf config set git.integration_branch ... --project`, or `migrate-personal`, creates an un-ignored `.context-forge.local.toml` that a normal `git add -A` commits. That is exactly the leak the Value section (line 23) says this slice prevents.

Two lighter fixes are available:
- have `ConfigManager.set` / `migrate-personal` ensure the ignore entry when they first create the personal file; or
- extend the new `cf check` rule to flag a personal file that isn't gitignored (for example via `git check-ignore`).

findings.title: The `cf init` gitignore step's placement is unspecified, a claim about existing patterns is wrong, and the failure handling contradicts init's conventions
findings.description:
- **Placement:** `cf init` skips all setup steps under `--lite` (`init.ts:85`). Walkthrough steps 1 and 3 (`cf init --lite`, then `cat .gitignore`) only work if the gitignore step runs outside that block. The design never says this, so an implementer following the existing structure would put it inside the block and step 3 would fail.
- **Wrong claim:** line 32 says the step reuses "the pattern already used for personal ignores". No such pattern exists. Line 159 itself confirms that no gitignore logic exists, and I found none in `packages/`.
- **Failure handling:** line 151 says aborting on failure is "consistent with how other `cf init` file-write failures are already handled". In fact every post-registration setup step in `init.ts` (guides at 87-97, commands at 100-105, IDE at 108-116) catches the error and continues with `warn(...)`. Aborting would be the odd one out. Pick catch-and-warn to match, or justify the abort.

findings.title: No tests are named for the collision path, partial-failure path, or `cf init`
Proportionality: the migration machinery is heavier than a registry with one personal key needs
MCP tool descriptions go stale and aren't in scope
findings.description:
Agents read tool descriptions verbatim:
- `config_get`'s description says "Resolution order: project config → user config → built-in default" (`configTools.ts:15`).
- `config_set` says `"project" writes to project-level config` (`configTools.ts:66`).

After this slice both are wrong for personal keys, and the `'project-personal'` source value is undocumented. Technical Scope (line 34) and Development Approach step 7 only add a `configPaths` field. Add the description updates.

Two smaller points:
- `configPaths` appears only in the no-key list response (`configTools.ts:36-43`). Line 72 says "config_get response includes both project config paths", so say "list mode".
- The `cf config` description "(get, set, unset)" (`config.ts:64`) should also gain `migrate-personal`.

findings.title: `migrate-personal`'s `--project` form doesn't match its sibling subcommands
findings.description: `get`, `set` and `unset` all declare `-p, --project [id]`, where a bare flag resolves from the current directory (`config.ts:68,110,140`). They resolve through `resolveConfigProjectPath`, which also accepts an unregistered directory. Line 193 specifies `-p, --project <id>` (value required). Use `[id]` and the same resolver, so `cf config migrate-personal` works the same way inside a project.

findings.title: The design adds a dependency the slice plan doesn't list
findings.description: The frontmatter declares `dependencies: [914]`, but the slice plan entry (900-slices line 36) says "Dependencies: none". The design's reasoning is sound and 914 is complete, so there's no harm. Consider updating the plan entry to match.

findings.title: The "every current caller" list is incomplete
findings.description: `ConfigManager` is also used by `reviewGate.ts`, `GuideManager.ts`, MCP `guideTools.ts` and `workflowTools.ts`. None of them need changes, so the conclusion holds, but the list isn't exhaustive as claimed.

findings.title: The claim about "default behavior" before the 916 fix doesn't match current code
findings.description: Line 138 implies that writing to project scope was the default only before the 916 fix. Today, `resolveScopeAndPath` still defaults to `scope: 'project'` whenever `--global` is absent (`config.ts:53-58`). Bare `cf config set git.integration_branch X` therefore writes project scope now, and will hit the personal file after this slice. The behaviour is fine; the background description is just inaccurate.

findings.title: A malformed or truncated personal file isn't covered as a failure mode
findings.description:
`writeToml` is a plain non-atomic `writeFile` (`ConfigManager.ts:33-36`). A kill mid-write, or a hand edit, can leave `.context-forge.local.toml` unparseable. `readToml` then throws on every read of that key, and `list()` iterates every key (`ConfigManager.ts:206-217`), so it throws too and `cf config get` with no key fails entirely.

The same risk exists for the shared file today. The difference is that the personal file is gitignored, so `git checkout` can't restore it. One sentence naming the recovery (delete the file, or re-set the key) would close this.
